points.title: 早期音乐探索
points.description: 勋伯格出生于维也纳的一个犹太家庭，早年自学音乐，后师从亚历山大·冯·策姆林斯基。这一时期他创作了《升华之夜》等早期作品，开始探索晚期浪漫主义风格。他同时从事银行工作，并在维也纳的音乐圈中结识了古斯塔夫·马勒等作曲家。这一阶段的作品显示出瓦格纳和勃拉姆斯的影响，同时也开始展现其独特的和声语言和对传统调性的突破尝试。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Vienna to a Jewish family, Schoenberg was largely self-taught in music before studying with Alexander von Zemlinsky. During this period, he composed works like 'Transfigured Night' and began exploring late Romantic styles. He worked as a banker while networking with composers like Gustav Mahler in Vienna's musical circles. His compositions from this phase show the influence of Wagner and Brahms while beginning to display his unique harmonic language and attempts to break with traditional tonality.

points.title: 突破与创新
points.description: 1901年至1911年间，勋伯格在柏林度过了一段重要时期。他创作了《佩利亚斯与梅丽桑德》等关键作品，并发展了他的'发展性变奏'技巧。1908年，他创作了《空中花园之歌》，标志着他完全放弃调性，成为无调性音乐的先驱。1909年，他创作了震惊乐坛的《期待》，一部独幕表现主义歌剧。这一时期他还开始教授私人学生，包括阿尔班·伯格和安东·韦伯恩，形成了后来被称为'第二维也纳学派'的核心团体。
points.descriptionEn: Between 1901 and 1911, Schoenberg spent a crucial period in Berlin. He composed key works like 'Pelléas et Mélisande' and developed his technique of 'developing variation.' In 1908, he composed 'Gurre-Lieder,' marking his complete abandonment of tonality, making him a pioneer of atonal music. In 1909, he created the shocking 'Erwartung,' a one-act expressionist opera. During this time, he also began teaching private students, including Alban Berg and Anton Webern, forming the core of what would later be known as the 'Second Viennese School.'

points.title: 理论建设
points.description: 1911年，勋伯格回到维也纳，发表了具有里程碑意义的著作《和声学理论》，系统阐述了他的无调性音乐理论。这一时期他创作了《五首管弦乐小品》等重要作品，并开始探索十二音技法的前身。第一次世界大战期间，他应征入伍，但继续音乐创作。战后，他于1919年创立'私人音乐表演学校'，致力于教授他的新音乐理念。1923年，他正式提出十二音作曲体系，彻底改变了20世纪音乐的发展方向。
points.descriptionEn: Returning to Vienna in 1911, Schoenberg published his seminal work 'Harmonielehre,' systematically expounding his theories of atonal music. During this period, he composed important works like 'Five Pieces for Orchestra' and began exploring precursors to his twelve-tone technique. During World War I, he served in the military but continued composing. After the war, he founded the 'Private Musical Performance School' in 1919 to teach his new musical concepts. In 1923, he formally introduced the twelve-tone composition system, fundamentally changing the direction of 20th-century music.

points.title: 教学巅峰
points.description: 1925年，勋伯格应邀担任柏林艺术学院教授，这是他职业生涯的巅峰时期。他进一步完善了十二音技法，创作了《钢琴组曲》等代表作。这一时期的学生包括汉斯·艾斯勒和尼基什·胡萨克等。然而，随着纳粹势力在德国的崛起，他的音乐被贴上'堕落艺术'的标签，作品被禁止演出。1933年，当纳粹上台后，他被解除了教职，被迫离开德国，标志着他欧洲生涯的结束。
points.descriptionEn: In 1925, Schoenberg was appointed professor at the Berlin Academy of Arts, marking the peak of his career. He further developed his twelve-tone technique, composing representative works like the 'Piano Suite.' His students during this period included Hanns Eisler and Nikos Hatzakos. However, as Nazi power grew in Germany, his music was labeled 'degenerate art' and performances were banned. When the Nazis came to power in 1933, he was dismissed from his teaching position and forced to leave Germany, marking the end of his European career.

points.title: 流亡岁月
points.description: 1933年，勋伯格移居巴黎，短暂停留后于1934年移居美国，最初在波士顿定居。1935年，他接受了洛杉矶加利福尼亚大学的教职。这一时期他完成了《摩西与亚伦》等重要作品，并继续发展他的十二音理论。尽管面临语言障碍和文化适应的挑战，他仍保持创作活力，并培养了美国新一代作曲家。他的流亡经历深刻影响了他的创作，作品中流露出对欧洲传统的怀念和对新环境的思考。
points.descriptionEn: In 1933, Schoenberg moved to Paris, and after a brief stay, relocated to the United States in 1934, initially settling in Boston. In 1935, he accepted a teaching position at the University of California, Los Angeles. During this period, he completed important works like 'Moses and Aron' and continued developing his twelve-tone theory. Despite facing language barriers and cultural adaptation challenges, he maintained his creative vitality and mentored a new generation of American composers. His exile experience profoundly influenced his compositions, revealing nostalgia for European traditions and reflections on his new environment.

points.title: 晚年成就
points.description: 1945年后，勋伯格在洛杉矶度过了他生命的最后岁月。他继续创作和教学，完成了《钢琴协奏曲》等重要作品。这一时期他获得了多项荣誉，包括美国艺术与科学院院士称号。尽管健康状况逐渐恶化，他仍坚持创作，直到1951年去世。他的晚年作品显示出对宗教和哲学主题的深入探索，同时继续完善十二音技法。他在美国培养的学生，包括约翰·凯奇和卢·哈里森等，将他的理念传播到更广阔的音乐世界。
points.descriptionEn: After 1945, Schoenberg spent his final years in Los Angeles. He continued composing and teaching, completing important works like the 'Piano Concerto.' During this period, he received numerous honors, including membership in the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. Despite declining health, he persisted in composing until his death in 1951. His late works show deep exploration of religious and philosophical themes while continuing to refine his twelve-tone technique. His American students, including John Cage and Lou Harrison, spread his ideas to a broader musical world.

supporter.zh: 勋伯格被誉为20世纪音乐革命的核心人物，他彻底打破了传统调性体系，开创了无调性和十二音音乐的新纪元。支持者认为他是一位勇敢的创新者，在音乐史上具有里程碑式的意义。他的理论体系为现代音乐发展提供了坚实基础，影响了无数作曲家。同时，他作为教师培养了一代重要作曲家，包括伯格和韦伯恩，形成了'第二维也纳学派'，对20世纪音乐教育产生了深远影响。
supporter.en: Schoenberg is hailed as a central figure in the 20th-century musical revolution who completely shattered traditional tonal systems, pioneering atonal and twelve-tone music. Supporters view him as a courageous innovator of landmark significance in music history. His theoretical system provided a solid foundation for modern music development, influencing countless composers. As a teacher, he mentored a generation of important composers including Berg and Webern, forming the 'Second Viennese School' and profoundly impacting 20th-century music education.

critic.zh: 批评者认为勋伯格的音乐过于理论化和抽象，缺乏情感表达和可听性。他们指责他的十二音技法导致音乐变得机械和公式化，失去了音乐的本质魅力。一些评论家认为他的创新是矫枉过正，忽视了音乐的传统价值和听众的接受度。此外，他的教学方式也被批评为过于专制，不容置疑。还有人指出，尽管他声称自己的音乐是'逻辑的必然发展'，但实际上更多是个人偏好的产物，而非音乐进化的必然结果。
critic.en: Critics argue that Schoenberg's music is overly theoretical and abstract, lacking emotional expression and accessibility. They accuse his twelve-tone technique of making music mechanical and formulaic, losing the essential charm of music. Some commentators believe his innovations were excessive, neglecting traditional musical values and audience reception. Additionally, his teaching style has been criticized as authoritarian and dogmatic. Others point out that while he claimed his music was a 'logical necessity,' it was often more a product of personal preference than an inevitable evolution of music.

objective.zh: 从历史和文化视角看，勋伯格被公认为现代音乐史上的关键转折点。他的作品和理论不仅改变了音乐创作方式，也深刻影响了整个20世纪的艺术思潮。尽管他的音乐在当时和后世都引发争议，但他对音乐语言的扩展和对传统规则的挑战，使他成为现代主义艺术的代表人物。在流行文化中，他常被描绘为音乐界的'叛逆者'或'革命者'，这种形象虽然简化了其复杂性，但也反映了他在音乐史上的变革性地位。他的遗产至今仍在音乐理论、作曲实践和教育领域持续产生影响。
objective.en: From a historical and cultural perspective, Schoenberg is widely recognized as a pivotal turning point in modern music history. His works and theories not only transformed musical composition but also profoundly influenced artistic trends throughout the 20th century. Despite controversies surrounding his music both then and now, his expansion of musical language and challenge to traditional rules establish him as a representative figure of modernist art. In popular culture, he is often depicted as a 'rebel' or 'revolutionary' in music, a simplified image that nonetheless reflects his transformative status in music history. His legacy continues to influence music theory, composition, and education to this day.

self.zh: 我的音乐不是由我发明的，而是由我发现的。它是逻辑的必然发展。
self.en: My music is not invented by me, but discovered by me. It is a logical necessity.

others.zh: 勋伯格是音乐史上最伟大的革命者，他摧毁了旧世界，却未能创造一个新世界。
others.en: Schoenberg was the greatest revolutionary in music history; he destroyed the old world but failed to create a new one.
